Amanda — forwarding our internal preflight checklist and a short notes doc for security. I pasted the most actionable items below so IT/security can triage quickly.

Key checklist (minimal on‑prem prerequisites — action items for GreenBridge):
1) Network & connectivity
   - Provide network diagram (attached: greenbridge-network-diagram-v1.png).
   - Edge egress: outbound TLS to our control plane endpoints (redwood-control.redwood.ai:443); list of IP ranges included in the attached PDF.
   - Allow bi-directional TCP:443 from the deployment hosts to the Redis/metrics endpoints (see PDF).
2) DNS & certs
   - Internal DNS entries for model-serving hostnames (we can provide target names).
   - TLS cert: either customer-managed cert (SAN entries) or we can use a cert rotated via your ACME integration.
3) Storage & logging
   - S3-compatible object store access for checkpoint/backup (VPC endpoints or IAM role).
   - Audit logs must be reachable to your SIEM (syslog/HTTPS); retained per your policy.
4) Access & IAM
   - Service account for install with SSH and temporary sudo (we use short-lived keys during deploy).
   - KMS/HSM integration details (if you require HSM, please provide vendor contact).
5) Compliance docs
   - We'll attach a 1‑page SOC2 summary and sample data retention policy for review (in PDF).

Attachments included: redwood-onprem-prereqs.pdf, greenbridge-network-diagram-v1.png

If IT can pre-validate the firewall rules and share a screenshot of the NAT/egress config, we can avoid surprises during install. I'll put a shared Drive folder in the HubSpot record for uploads.

Amanda / Camila — adding a few technical clarifications from the infra team so IT knows exactly what to check before the scheduled window. Please forward to whoever runs the firewall and NAT.

Short checklist for the infra team (technical specifics):
- IPs and ports: outbound to the control plane on TCP/443 to these ranges: 34.120.0.0/14, 35.201.64.0/18 (we will confirm/update in the shared drive).
- Persistent connections: the serving hosts will maintain long-lived TLS connections (keepalive) — ensure load balancers do not drop connections below 15s idle.
- KV cache and metrics: allow egress to metrics.redwood.ai:443 and redis.redwood.internal:6379 (if using private peering we can provide internal endpoints).
- MTU and jumbo frames: some on‑prem environments set 9000 MTU; our runtime is tolerant but please confirm path MTU >= 1500.
- Time sync: NTP must be reachable (pool.ntp.org or a corporate NTP). Certificate rotation fails without accurate time.
- DNS split‑horizon: if you use internal hostnames, provide forward/reverse records for the model-serving hostnames we will reference.

Optional but recommended:
- Test harness: we can run a low‑impact smoke test that generates short sequences to validate latency and egress. We just need a temporary service account and SSH during the test window.

If IT can paste firewall rules or a config excerpt into the Drive folder before Fri 8/13, I can pre-validate and reduce install time.

Thanks —
Dev Patel
